Yesterday the US government announced an update to the list of prohibited foreign-manufactured products, adding "advanced robotic devices", and an FCC spokesperson confirmed today that the ban also applies to robotic vacuum cleaners.

The robotic vacuum ban affects Roomba, Roborock and other well-known brands, but you can continue to use your existing products

When the Trump administration announced yesterday a ban on "advanced robotic devices" entering the US, the headlines focused on humanoid robots. But espionage does not need legs, and nor does the FCC's robot ban. FCC Director of Media Relations Katie Gorscak confirmed to The Verge that the ban will also cover robotic vacuum cleaners. The ban will not target the Roomba already in your home, and companies may continue to import and sell models that have already been approved. But the government claims future foreign robots pose a national security risk, and even robotic vacuum companies have suddenly been asked to commit to manufacturing in the US.

The FCC pointed out that advanced robotic devices carry national security risks, and this rule also applies to seemingly harmless products such as robotic vacuum cleaners and lawn mowers.

Unless a product is explicitly approved, or for example manufactured on US soil, it will not be allowed to be sold in the US.

The ban is expected to hit the robotic vacuum market particularly hard, as top brands such as Roomba, Roborock and Ecovacs are all owned by Chinese companies.

If you already own such a product, you can still use it today — the FCC is not going to come to your door and confiscate your robotic vacuum.

But depending on how the ban is enforced, the robotic vacuum market could see drastic changes in the short term. If all this sounds familiar, that is because the ban is strikingly similar to the wireless router ban imposed a few months ago.

Will you continue to use your existing robotic vacuum? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.
